authoredNote: The K2 rows (the delegation edges exist, target the literal keyword, confidence 1.0) were authored before the analyzer ran. The SOURCE row was RE-PINNED on 2026-10-05 by DERIV_EXPORTS_KOT4, and the change of mind is recorded in the rationale rather than quietly applied: the original expectation said `from: "constructor"`, which is the placeholder the M14 #419 K11 rule was written to remove. The fixture had pinned the defect, so the rule stayed half-implemented for a wave.
rationale: PINS the K2 gap: secondary-constructor delegation — super(...) and this(...) — is a call edge from the constructor. super/this are UNNAMED keyword children of constructor_delegation_call, so the receiver is read from node text; the target is the literal keyword (never guessed to a parent type, per the java G2 ruling). Confidence 1.0: delegation is structural syntax. DERIV_EXPORTS_KOT4 re-pinned the SOURCE from the literal `constructor` to the owning class `Derived`, and the forbid row below is what keeps the placeholder from coming back: `secondary_constructor`'s parent is the class_body, not the class_declaration, so the K11 rule's own implementation (`node.parent` -> name) silently failed for every secondary constructor in the corpus — measured at 60 edges over 405 files attributed to a symbol spelled `constructor`, which no Kotlin source can declare. The forbid row is the half that matters: without it the expectation alone would still have passed on the old behaviour if the edge had also been emitted with the class name.
